Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year - far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

Ramp is building institutional partnerships with top global strategy consulting firms that shape finance transformation and technology decisions for the CFOs and CEOs we serve. NOCD is the #1 telehealth provider for the treatment of obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). OCD is one of the most severe, prevalent, and misunderstood mental health conditions. NOCD creates access to online therapy for people with OCD through our telehealth platform. In the NOCD app, Members can quickly access and schedule live, face-to-face video therapy sessions with our national network of licensed Therapists that specialize in Exposure and Response Prevention Therapy (ERP) - considered the "gold standard" in OCD treatment.

Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

What You'll Own

• Lead product direction for major AI Neobank app areas.

• Work across insurance, payments, savings, investing, travel and other financial services.

• Drive launch quality, post-launch learning and continuous improvement.

• Help build a product culture focused on speed, clarity, user value and honest measurement.

What We're Looking For

• Strong experience leading digital product areas, not just individual features.

• Able to balance strategy, execution, UX, data, engineering and business outcomes.

• Strong judgement on prioritization, trade-offs and product sequencing.

• Experience leading or mentoring PMs / POs / cross-functional squads is a strong advantage.

• Comfortable with high ambiguity, fast changes and senior stakeholder pressure.

• Able to simplify complex financial products into usable journeys.

• Experience in fintech, insurance, payments, consumer apps or regulated products is a strong advantage.

The Kind of Builder We Want

• Can set direction and still go deep into details.

• Pushes teams to move faster without lowering product quality.

• Knows when to simplify, when to scale and when to say no.

• Can lead through clarity, not bureaucracy.

• Avoids false claims and understands that product impact usually comes from many iterations and teams.

This Role Is Not For

• Product leaders who only manage people and meetings.

• People who cannot go deep into product details.

• Candidates who are too slow for a high-growth environment.

• Leaders who push vanity metrics without understanding real user impact.

• People who need large teams before they can create progress.

2. Role-specific interview

title: AI Engineer
description:
About Board of Innovation

BOI partners with large, ambitious organizations to design and build applied AI products that create measurable business impact. We help enterprise and scale-up clients move beyond experimentation by embedding AI directly into their operations, decision-making, and products. Our work spans industries, but always centers on production-ready AI, strong engineering, and real-world adoption.
About the Role
We're looking for an AI Engineer to design and build the AI systems behind real, production-grade applications. This is applied engineering work: building agentic workflows, retrieval pipelines, and orchestration layers that integrate into business-critical environments and stand up to real-world use.
You'll take AI capabilities from idea to deployment, owning the full path including evaluation, observability, and the operational concerns that determine whether a system survives contact with users.
What You'll Do
You'll design, implement, and ship AI systems that automate work, support decisions, and unlock new workflows for enterprise clients. Day-to-day, that means building multi-step agents and tool-using LLM systems, wiring them into structured and unstructured data sources, and packaging them into services that other engineers and applications can consume safely.
You'll also own how we know our systems work. That includes evals, observability, and the feedback loops that let us iterate with confidence rather than guesswork. You'll work closely with engineers, strategists, and designers, and you'll be in client conversations from early scoping through delivery.
What You Bring
You have 3+ years of experience shipping AI-powered systems in production, and a background in computer science, math, physics, engineering, or another technical or scientific field. You're strong in Python and fluent in the patterns of modern LLM engineering: agents, MCP, skills, tool use, retrieval, structured outputs, and evals.
You're also a real software engineer underneath. CI/CD, testing, version control hygiene, and code quality matter to you, because they're what let you keep moving fast without things falling over. You understand how to balance accuracy, latency, cost, and maintainability, and you've debugged enough production systems to have opinions about it. You're comfortable wrapping AI logic into services that other engineers can consume without surprises.
How You Work
You treat AI as an engineering discipline. You care about observability, maintainability, and the underlying engineering that makes the interesting parts possible. You're at home in a consulting environment, where each engagement brings a new domain and a new set of constraints.
At BOI, you will work a lot with strategists, designers, and consultants, and most of your clients aren't technical. You're comfortable translating between business problems and technical solutions, and you can hold your own in a client room without a project manager running interference for you.
The field moves quickly, and so do we. New models, new tools, and new patterns show up constantly. You enjoy that pace, actively pull in what's useful, and bring it back to the team. You push back when something doesn't make sense, and you care about building systems that get used long after the kickoff energy fades.
Contract & Setup
We are open to both permanent employment and long-term contractor arrangements. The final setup will depend on your location, work authorization status, and local compliance requirements.
Interested?
If this sounds like a fit, apply with your CV and a short note on a system you've built that you're proud of. Bonus points for something we can actually look at!

CBRE is the world's largest commercial real estate services firm. Experience by Industrious is CBRE's global experience and hospitality business. The first thing someone experiences when they arrive at a building sets the tone for everything that follows. You're that first thing.

As a Lobby Ambassador, your job is to make arrivals and departures feel smooth, welcoming, and professional. You greet tenants by name, manage the visitor check-in process, answer questions about the building, and make sure the lobby always looks and feels the way it should.

This is a hospitality role grounded in consistency. The value you create isn't in occasional big moments - it's in showing up the same way every single day, so tenants know exactly what to expect when they walk through the door.

This is an in-person position that requires standing for extended periods of time.

WINNING IN THIS ROLE MEANS

• Every tenant is greeted by name. Every guest knows exactly where to go. Every arrival feels easy.

• The lobby is always clean, organized, and ready. Facilities and IT issues are escalated before anyone has to ask.

• Your reliability is a given. The team knows you'll be there, you'll be on, and things will be handled.

• Tenants trust you with their preferences and feedback because you've shown them you act on it.

• You're a positive presence in the building. People are glad to see you.

YOU'LL LOVE THIS ROLE AND SUCCEED AT IT IF

• You notice things. When the lobby needs attention, when a guest looks confused, when a package is sitting unclaimed - you see it, and you take care of it.

• You're calm in busy environments. A busy morning, a complicated visitor check-in, an unexpected question - none of it rattles you. You've got a process and you trust it.

• Being on your feet works for you. You're not sitting behind a desk waiting for things to happen. You're present, engaged, and active throughout the day.

NOT THE RIGHT FIT IF

title: Senior Power Controls Engineer
description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

Anduril is seeking an experienced Power Controls Engineer to develop and implement advanced control algorithms for high-performance power electronic systems. We're looking for someone with deep expertise in control system modeling and simulation - particularly in Simulink and PLECS - who can take a controls concept from simulation through hardware validation. This individual will own the control architecture for DC/DC converters, inverters, and motor drives built around discrete SiC and GaN power stages, and will work closely with power hardware and firmware engineers to deliver tightly integrated, high-reliability systems for defense and aerospace applications.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

• Design, simulate, and validate closed-loop control algorithms for switch-mode power converters and inverters using Simulink and/or PLECS.

• Controls for 3-phase AC systems, with and without a switched Neutral

• Develop plant models and controller architectures (voltage-mode, current-mode, sensorless FOC, etc.) for multi-kW power stages utilizing discrete SiC and GaN FETs.

• Perform stability analysis, loop shaping, and compensator design to meet transient response, efficiency, and EMI targets.

• Collaborate with power hardware engineers on gate drive tuning, dead-time optimization, and switching-loss characterization of wide-bandgap devices.

• Support model-based code generation workflows and work with firmware engineers to translate control designs into embedded implementations.

• Define and execute hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) and power-hardware-in-the-loop (PHIL) test plans to validate control performance against system requirements.

• Contribute to trade studies on converter topology, modulation strategy, and control bandwidth as they relate to size, weight, power, and thermal constraints.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

• BS in Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, or related discipline.

• 8+ years of experience designing and tuning digital control loops for power electronic converters (DC/DC, DC/AC, or motor drives).

• Proficiency in Simulink and/or PLECS for control system modeling, simulation, and analysis.

• Strong foundation in control theory - z-domain and s-domain design, bode analysis, state-space methods, and discrete-time implementation considerations.

• Hands-on experience with discrete SiC and/or GaN FET-based power stages in the multi-kW range.

• Familiarity with military or aerospace environments and standards such as MIL-STD-461, 464, 810, or DO-160.

• Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

• MS/PhD with a focus in power electronics controls or control systems.

• Experience writing embedded firmware (C/C++) for microcontrollers or DSPs used in power converter control (e.g., TI C2000, STM32).

• Familiarity with auto-code generation from Simulink (Embedded Coder) or similar model-based design toolchains.

• Experience with real-time HIL platforms (e.g., Typhoon HIL, dSPACE, OPAL-RT).

• Knowledge of advanced modulation techniques (SVM, DPWM) and their impact on switching losses in wide-bandgap devices.

• Design-for-Reliability practices including DFMEA.

• Experience with EMI mitigation strategies at the controls and layout level.

title: Technical Writer
description:
TL;DR: Most companies treat documentation as a help centre. At Lovable it's part of the product. Millions of people learn to build software from our docs, and so do the AI agents working for them: the Lovable agent suggests pages, coding tools read them, and our assistants answer from them. You'll be our second technical writer, with product areas of your own from the start and a seat at every launch, and you'll help work out something nobody has fully worked out yet: what documentation should be when its readers are people and agents, and the product changes every day.

Why Lovable?

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we're just getting started.

We're building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME's 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe's fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.

What we're looking for

- You've spent 3+ years documenting software products, and you can show us pages that get a reader to the outcome without re-reading.

- You already write with AI: for research, drafting and checking, not just polish. You know what it gets wrong and you catch it.

- You test what you document. You'd rather try the feature and read the source than take someone's word for it, and when something's broken or confusing, you say so.

- You're at home in docs-as-code: Git, Markdown and pull requests.

- You ask engineers and PMs specific questions, and when documenting a feature shows it won't make sense to users, you raise it early, with reasons.

- Preferred: you've shipped docs weekly at a startup or scale-up, finding out what changed yourself. You've written for AI readers, or you're curious about it. You have UX writing or content design experience, or an interest in it. You can read code well enough to check how a feature actually behaves; writing code is not required.

What you'll do

- Drive, don't wait. Features land every day, and bigger launches several times a month. You find out what's shipping before anyone tells you, and the docs are ready the day it ships.

- Own it end to end. Work a feature out from the code and the product, write the page, verify it in Lovable, ship it, and keep it true as the product moves.

- Care about the reader more than the feature. Our docs come with data: what people can't find, what the assistant couldn't answer, what support hears. You use it to decide what to write next.

- Make the product better, not just explain it. Documenting a feature means using it end to end. You'll find the confusing label or the broken step and get it fixed before launch.

- Write for three readers on one page. The non-technical builder, the developer, and the AI agent working on their behalf.

- Build something that outlasts the week. AI drafts a lot of our pages. The human work is judgement: what a feature needs, what the engineer didn't mention, and the checks that keep hundreds of pages correct.

- Where you'll start:

- Enterprise. Identity and access, governance, audit, data residency: the pages a security team reads before they sign.

title: Collecte de données vocales – France et outre-mer
description:
En quoi consiste le projet ?
L’objectif de ce projet vise à collecter des enregistrements vocaux de personnes de langue maternelle française afin d’améliorer les technologies d’assistant vocal.
Description de la tâche :
Pour ce projet, nous recherchons une grande variété de locuteurs natifs de langue française (France et outre-mer) avec divers accents régionaux. Les participants enregistreront de courtes phrases d’activation et des énoncés scriptés généralement utilisés lors d’interactions avec un assistant vocal, en suivant les instructions fournies.
Qui peut participer à l’étude ?
Pour participer, vous devez remplir les conditions suivantes :

• Avoir 18 ans ou plus.

• Être né(e) et vivre en France ou outre-mer.

• Être de langue maternelle française, de n’importe quelle région de France ou outre-mer.

• Avoir une bonne maîtrise de l’anglais, car toutes les instructions du projet seront en anglais.

• Être en mesure d’utiliser un téléphone portable pour ce projet.

• Pouvoir utiliser un casque filaire ou le microphone de l’appareil pour enregistrer des phrases.

•
Avoir accès à un environnement intérieur calme pour effectuer les enregistrements.

Notes:

• Dans le cadre de ce projet, nous recherchons des participants issus de groupes démographiques spécifiques afin de contribuer au développement d’une technologie impartiale qui soit représentative de tous. Certains groupes sont déjà complets, mais nous recherchons toujours des voix masculines avec des accents du Nord, du Nord-est, du Sud-ouest et du Sud-est de la France.

• Nous recherchons aussi des participants issus d’outre-mer: Guadeloupe (971), Martinique (972), Guyane (973), La Réunion (974), Mayotte (976), Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon (975), Saint-Barthélemy (977), Saint-Martin (978), Wallis-et-Futuna (986), Polynésie française (987), Nouvelle-Calédonie (988), Terres australes et antarctiques françaises (984) et Clipperton (989).

Veuillez noter que ce projet est également ouvert aux participants âgés de 7 à 17 ans . Pour plus de détails, veuillez vous référer à ce formulaire :Gardenia Speech Collection - France (Minors) | DataForce Community
Où le projet a-t-il lieu ?
C’est un projet entièrement à distance. Vous pouvez participer depuis n’importe où en France ou outre-mer.
Combien de temps dure-t-il ?
La durée estimée de la tâche d’enregistrement est de 30 minutes.
Quel est le montant de la rémunération ?
Vous recevrez $ 33 USD pour vos livrables entièrement terminés et acceptés.
Programme général de prime de parrainage
Nous offrons une prime de parrainage de $ 15 USD pour chaque participant adulte que vous recommandez pour le projet et qui le termine avec succès.
Comment parrainer quelqu’un :
- Partagez ce lien d’inscription avec vos amis et votre famille
- Lors de leur inscription, ils doivent répondre « Referral» (Recommandation) à la question « How did you find out about this opportunity? » (Comment avez-vous pris connaissance de cette opportunité ?) et indiquer votre nom et votre adresse e-mail dans les champs : Prénom, Nom et adresse e-mail.
Comme mode de paiement, nous proposons le Virement bancaire, PayPal et la Carte cadeau , selon votre préférence.
Veuillez noter que notre équipe d’assurance qualité examinera toutes les soumissions pour s’assurer qu’elles respectent les exigences spécifiques du projet. L’équipe du projet vous enverra des commentaires une fois le processus de contrôle qualité terminé.
Des questions ou des doutes ?
Si vous avez des doutes ou des questions, n’hésitez pas à nous contacter à:

title: Senior Accountant
description:
Posit is a Public Benefit Corporation and Certified B Corp on a mission to create open-source software for data science, scientific research, and technical communication - and we’re building a company designed to thrive for 100 years.
Our Accounting team keeps the company’s books accurate, timely, and audit-ready, and partners with Finance, Payroll, and the business to turn financial data into decisions. We value sound judgment, clear communication, and continuous improvement, and we invest in automation so our people spend their time on analysis and problem solving rather than manual work. We’re looking for a Senior Accountant to join the team, reporting to an Accounting Manager and working closely with FP&A, Tax, Payroll, AP/AR, Engineering/IT, and our external auditors.
YOUR IMPACT
Why this role exists: to keep Posit’s books accurate, timely, and audit-ready - and to raise the standard for how the Accounting team works. You are singularly responsible for:

• Prepare accurate, timely financial statements, reconciliation schedules, and supporting analysis (flux, variance, and trend) for your assigned areas. Serve as the subject matter expert for those areas, including researching and documenting the technical accounting positions behind complex or non-routine transactions.

• Lead accounting projects and system changes from plan through delivery.

• Identify and implement improvements to accounting practices, including automation that delivers data faster and reduces risk across teams.

• Own internal controls for your areas; identify process or control deficiencies, design and implement solutions, and raise the standard for how the team works.

• Collaborate well with others, stay positive under pressure, welcome feedback, and contribute to the department’s shared goals.

HOW YOU’LL COLLABORATE
You’ll be the senior voice for the areas you own, working across Posit to keep the close on schedule and the controls strong:

• Partner with FP&A, Payroll, Tax, AP/AR, and Engineering/IT on data flows, system changes, internal controls, and month-end close dependencies.

• Support internal and external audits and the testing of people, process, and system controls.

• Mentor less experienced teammates with their questions by reviewing their work and explaining your thinking, and present regularly to the team and stakeholders.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING

• Has independently run month-end close and prepared financial statements for multiple areas, including complex or non-routine transactions, with limited review.

• Hands-on NetSuite experience (or a related ERP): journal entries, reconciliations, saved searches, and running the close in the system.

• Advanced Excel skills, including complex formulas (lookups, nested logic, pivots, and array formulas) for reconciliations and analysis.

• Day-to-day experience using an AI tool for analysis, automation, or documentation, with sound judgment in validating its output.

• Strong working knowledge of US GAAP and the ability to explain accounting decisions clearly, with the reasoning behind them.

• Understanding of people, process, and system controls, and a track record of leading a project or process improvement.

title: Senior Site Reliability Engineer
description:
About Mozn
MOZN is a leading Enterprise AI company enabling organizations to make informed decisions in two critical domains: Financial Crime Prevention and Enterprise Knowledge Intelligence.

We’re a diverse, collaborative team of innovators united by a shared purpose: to build AI that delivers tangible business value, builds trust, and empowers people and organizations with augmented intelligence. Our culture is built on the relentless pursuit of excellence and meaningful impact.

If you’re passionate about working alongside exceptional talent on world-class AI, and you want the autonomy and runway to do the best work of your career, join us in shaping the future of intelligent enterprises.
About the role
We're hiring an AI Senior SRE: someone who carries a normal SRE workload - on-call rotation, incident response, root cause analysis, hands-on Kubernetes/cloud work - and builds the agentic layer that automates that workload over time. You are not exempt from operating production. You're the person best placed to know what should be automated, because you're the one doing it. This role exists because most reliability toil (triage, root-causing, remediation, SLO tracking, onboarding checks) is repetitive and well-defined enough to hand to an LLM-based agent with the right guardrails. Your job is to do the on-call/ops work like any SRE, then turn what you learn into agents - identify the workflow, build the agent, and earn the trust to let it act with increasing autonomy.
What you'll do

• Carry a normal on-call rotation and act as a hands-on responder: investigate, fix, and document incidents yourself, exactly like any SRE on the team - especially for workflows that don' t have an agent yet.

• Go deep on application-level reliability, not just infrastructure: read and debug service code, understand business logic well enough to find the real root cause, and ship fixes or PRs directly into application repos when the fix belongs in the app, not the platform.

• Design, build, and ship LLM-based agents (using tools like Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, or Kimi K2/K3) that plug into our existing stack: Kubernetes, cloud APIs, Prometheus/Grafana/ELK/Datadog, PagerDuty/Slack.

• Define the "tool" interface each agent needs - the specific APIs, scripts, and read/write actions - and build safe wrappers around them.

• Set clear guardrails for every agent: what it may do autonomously vs. what it must propose for human approval, with a bias toward human-in-the-loop until an agent has earned trust.

• Own agent evaluation - define what "correct" and "safe" look like per agent, and build test/backtest suites against real historical incidents.

• Continuously tune prompts, context, and tool schemas as an agent' s scope grows.

• Partner with the SRE/platform team to find good agent candidates: repetitive, well-scoped, auditable workflows.

• Report on agent impact - MTTD/MTTR/MTTX movement, false positive/negative rates, and engineer-hours of toil removed.

• Keep a security- and compliance-first posture: audit trails for every autonomous action, least-privilege access to production, and alignment with Saudi data residency/regulatory requirements.

Requirements

• 3+ years building production software with LLMs - agentic workflows, tool/function calling, multi-step planning, RAG - not just personal use of a chat assistant.

• Hands-on experience shipping real work with an agentic coding tool such as Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, or Kimi K2/K3.

• Strong Python (or similar) for building agent tooling, API wrappers, and orchestration.

• Real, hands-on SRE experience: comfortable being a primary on-call responder, running incident response, and doing root cause analysis under pressure - not just familiar with the concepts.

• Application-level debugging skill, not just infra: able to read a service' s codebase, trace a failure back to the actual line/logic causing it, and ship a fix yourself - SRE work here isn' t limited to restarting pods or scal

title: Medical Science Liaison - Rare Disease
description:
POSITION SUMMARY:

 

The Medical Science Liaison (MSL), Rare Disease is a field-based scientific expert and a key scientific resource for clinicians, academic institutions, and professional organizations in the Rare Disease community. This individual builds relationships with Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs), leads scientific exchange on Natera's Rare Disease test, and brings field insights back to Rare Disease leadership. The MSL works closely with the Rare Disease Sales, Marketing, and Medical teams to help bring the test to more patients. This role operates with a high degree of autonomy and reports to the Director of MSLs, Rare Disease.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Provide scientific and clinical presentations on Natera products, with a focus on Rare Disease, and respond to customer requests for information about marketed and developing products.

• Develop, maintain, and manage relationships with KOLs from the Rare Disease community and other relevant healthcare professionals.

• Capture field insights on clinical practice, unmet needs, and market dynamics, and share them with Rare Disease leadership.

• Serve as a medical and scientific resource for the Natera Sales and Marketing teams, and collaborate with Marketing to develop educational materials for healthcare providers and patients.

• Participate in clinical research, data analysis, and scientific writing.

• Work with PHI in paper and electronic form. Complete HIPAA/PHI privacy, general policy and procedure compliance, and security training within the first 30 days of hire, and keep Natera training requirements current.

• Performs other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS:

• Master's degree required, or a doctorate (PharmD, PhD, MD/DO, DNP), in a clinical or scientific field with relevant knowledge of Rare Disease.

• Prior experience as an MSL or in another field-based role highly preferred.

• Experience with the introduction of new clinical laboratory tests preferred.

• Must pass a post-offer criminal background check.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:

Technical:

• Knowledge of Rare Disease and relevant clinical sciences, with the ability to explain clinical laboratory test data to clinicians.

• Proficiency with user databases, Google Sheets, and Salesforce, including systems that contain PHI.

• Working knowledge of HIPAA, PHI, and medical compliance standards.

• Scientific writing and data analysis skills.

Behavioral:

• Independent thinker who works with autonomy and manages priorities in a field-based role.

• Persuasive communicator with an outgoing and confident demeanor.

• Collaborates with Sales, Marketing, and Medical teams, and builds credibility with clinicians and KOLs.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORK ENVIRONMENT:

Duties are performed in a field-based, remote-first setting, including a home office and customer sites such as clinics, academic institutions, and professional meetings. This position requires the ability to use a computer keyboard, communicate over the telephone and by video, read printed and electronic material, and travel by air and car. title: Engineering Lead, Air Defense U.S. Air Force Portfolio
tags: AFS : Air Defense Engineering : Chief Engineering
description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril's Air Defense team develops, integrates, and fields autonomous systems that find, track, and defeat threats in the sky while keeping operators in control of engagement decisions. The team brings together Roadrunner, Sentry, Anvil, Pulsar, and Wisp with existing and third-party sensors and effectors through Lattice, creating a software-enabled family of systems for the modern battlespace. As control of the air becomes more contested, these networked capabilities give warfighters the awareness and response options needed to protect forces against rapidly evolving UAS threats.

ABOUT THE JOB

The U.S. Air Force is one of Anduril's largest and fastest-growing air defense customers, and the work has moved well past demonstrations. The portfolio runs programs of record, multi-year IDIQs, and recurring sustainment at the same time, and installation defense is scaling from individual sites toward a service-wide posture. The technical scope is broadening with it, across sensors, effectors, command and control, tactical networks, and accreditation boundaries.

Four kinds of work run in parallel. Permanent installations defend flightlines and test ranges on base infrastructure under a government accreditation posture, which makes power, networking, cyber compliance, and data handling as much of the engineering as sensors and effectors. Deployable kits ship on short notice and have to work on arrival, including in environments cold enough to change how the hardware behaves. Rapidly relocatable passive detection pushes the kill chain well past the base perimeter and into the theater air picture through tactical data links. And part of the portfolio executes inside special access environments, where the engineering includes constraining what the system is permitted to disclose.

You are the engineering lead across all of it. You own the technical baseline for the delivered configurations in the portfolio: the architecture, the interfaces to Anduril and third-party sensors and effectors, the networks underneath them, the accreditation scope, and the verification approach that determines whether any of it is ready. Where individual programs carry their own systems engineers, you hold the picture that spans them and settle the technical questions that fall between owners.

The work is broad by design. A given week might be reconciling environmental requirements that conflict across a contract and a test plan, defining the interface to a partner's fielded command and control, writing the technical content behind a proposal, or standing on a flightline because a site is not performing and the answer is not in the logs. The portfolio is growing faster than its engineering bench, so the role carries real latitude over where the engineering effort goes.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Own the technical baseline. Architecture, interface set, and verification approach for the delivered configurations across the portfolio. Set the baseline for each, and update it when field evidence shows the current one is incomplete or wrong. Own the certification and accreditation scope where it applies, working with the teams responsible for those functions.
